_comment: EPA waiver resolutions slice 4 (v364). The two pairs on each of H.J.Res. 88 and H.J.Res. 89 of the 119th — states_federal_power and cost_living — that printed nothing under their rows. Neither pair stores a `did`, so each line is written only from its own mapping rationale (quoted here as the cited migration wrote it) and the resolution's stored summary and title; `term` is the stored words the line carries and `termIn` names the field. Both resolutions are public law (the stored status is enacted), so each line reads as done and, like the lines already on these resolutions, carries no tally. `measures` holds every mapping on the two acts. No score, weight, mapping or key is read from or written to here.

rows.line: Repealed the waiver that let California set stricter vehicle emission standards than the national floor, narrowing that state authority.
rows.term: stricter vehicle emission standards than the national floor

source.rationale: Repeals the federal waiver that let California set stricter vehicle emission standards than the national floor; a yea narrows that state authority, so it is recorded as cutting against state power.

rows.line: Removed the rising zero-emission sales requirement in the adopting states, so the mix of new vehicles offered there is set by the market.

source.rationale: Removes the requirement that a rising share of new vehicle sales be zero-emission in the states that adopted the California rule, so the mix of new vehicles offered for sale there is set by the market rather than by the mandate schedule. A yea lifts that constraint on what a buyer can choose from.

rows.line: Repealed the federal waiver that let California set stricter heavy-truck standards than the national floor, narrowing that state authority.
rows.term: stricter heavy-truck standards than the national floor

source.rationale: Repeals the federal waiver that let California set stricter heavy-truck standards than the national floor; a yea narrows that state authority, so it is recorded as cutting against state power.

rows.line: Ended the zero-emission share required of new trucks sold in the adopting states, leaving fleet purchasers free to buy conventional trucks.

source.rationale: Ends the requirement that a rising share of new medium- and heavy-duty trucks sold in the adopting states be zero-emission, leaving fleet purchasers free to buy conventional trucks. A yea removes that purchase requirement from the freight chain.

H.J.Res. 88|119.title: Providing for congressional disapproval of the Environmental Protection Agency waiver for the California Advanced Clean Cars II regulations
H.J.Res. 88|119.summary: A Congressional Review Act resolution revoking the EPA waiver that let California require rising zero-emission-vehicle sales (the Advanced Clean Cars II rule) adopted by a dozen other states. Enacted 2025-06-12.

issues.rationale: Repeals the waiver behind California's EV sales mandate; a yea rolls back a major state climate rule.

Revokes the Clean Air Act waiver behind California's Advanced Clean Cars II rule, ending the requirement that a rising share of new vehicles sold be zero-emission in California and in the dozen states that adopted it. A yea keeps internal-combustion vehicles saleable in those markets.
Uses the Congressional Review Act to strike a federal waiver/rule.

Removes the requirement that a rising share of new vehicle sales be zero-emission in the states that adopted the California rule, so the mix of new vehicles offered for sale there is set by the market rather than by the mandate schedule. A yea lifts that constraint on what a buyer can choose from.
Repeals the federal waiver that let California set stricter vehicle emission standards than the national floor; a yea narrows that state authority, so it is recorded as cutting against state power.

H.J.Res. 89|119.title: Providing for congressional disapproval of the Environmental Protection Agency waiver for the California Advanced Clean Trucks regulations
H.J.Res. 89|119.summary: A Congressional Review Act resolution revoking the EPA waiver behind California's Advanced Clean Trucks rule, which required rising zero-emission sales of medium- and heavy-duty trucks. Enacted 2025-06-12.

issues.rationale: Repeals the waiver behind California's zero-emission truck mandate; a yea rolls back a major state climate rule.

Revokes the Clean Air Act waiver behind California's Advanced Clean Trucks rule, ending the requirement that a rising share of new medium- and heavy-duty truck sales be zero-emission. A yea removes that limit on conventional truck sales.
Uses the Congressional Review Act to strike a federal waiver/rule.

Ends the requirement that a rising share of new medium- and heavy-duty trucks sold in the adopting states be zero-emission, leaving fleet purchasers free to buy conventional trucks. A yea removes that purchase requirement from the freight chain.
Repeals the federal waiver that let California set stricter heavy-truck standards than the national floor; a yea narrows that state authority, so it is recorded as cutting against state power.
